finding.title: Two fully successful concurrent run_once refreshes can leave permanently mixed output generations
finding.mechanism: run_once builds each output from its own as_of_ms, then writes latest.json, audit_latest.json, anata_latest.json via three independent atomic_write_json calls; no shared generation lock or publication commit. Per-file os.replace atomicity does not make the three-file set atomic.
finding.fixture: tmp_path local_dir; seed archive with one valid ETF FlowObservation (effective=10*DAY, available=observed=11*DAY, source=fixture, source_record_id=day11, value=100, provenance={collector:fixture}). Run A with network=False,external_jsonl=(),as_of_ms=10*DAY and B with same local_dir and as_of_ms=12*DAY. Instrument runner.atomic_write_json with thread events: A writes latest A and pauses; B writes latest B,audit B,handoff B and returns success; A resumes, writes audit A,handoff A and returns success.
expected_assertions: Both run_once calls return without error and archive remains exactly one valid row, with unchanged provenance/available_at/observed_at.
All three final files must represent one coherent generation, or a reader must detect a mismatch and fail closed.
Source ordering predicts permanent latest.json=B, audit_latest.json=A, anata_latest.json=A; expected failure of the coherence assertion even though both runs succeed.
Re-run sequentially and confirm coherent generation; no duplicate archive admission. Verify both observation visibility cutoffs and strict JSON parse.
finding.distinct_from: 02:04 single successful refresh transient reader interleave; 10/13 output fault-injection failed write; 10/13 concurrent archive append race. This case has two successful refresh writers and a permanently inconsistent output set, without a reader interleaving or archive writes.
